options: A single file, built from a database project, that snapshots the intended state of a schema
A backup file containing the full row data of a database
A type of stored procedure used for deployment automation
A configuration file for SQL Server Agent jobs
questions.explain: Building a .sqlproj produces a DACPAC representing what the schema is intended to look like, not a change script.

questions.q: What does SqlPackage.exe do when deploying a DACPAC?
options: Compares the DACPAC's schema to the target database and generates and runs the statements needed to reconcile them
Copies the DACPAC file itself directly into the target database as binary data
Only validates the DACPAC without ever touching a live database
Deletes the target database and recreates it from scratch every time
questions.explain: SqlPackage performs a diff-and-apply operation, similar conceptually to Schema Compare, but automatically as a pipeline step.

questions.q: How does the migration-runner approach differ from DACPAC deployment?
options: It applies an ordered sequence of versioned migration scripts and tracks which have already run, rather than diffing a full schema snapshot against the target
It requires no tooling of any kind and is entirely manual
It only works for Oracle databases, not SQL Server
It is identical to DACPAC deployment, just under a different name
questions.explain: A migration runner asks 'which ordered steps haven't happened here yet' rather than diffing an end-state snapshot.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when might a migration-script approach be preferred over pure DACPAC deployment?
options: For data-transformation changes a schema-diff tool wouldn't know how to generate safely on its own
Whenever a database has fewer than ten tables
Only when using open-source database engines
Never — DACPAC deployment always fully replaces the need for migration scripts
questions.explain: Migration scripts give explicit control that matters most for changes involving actual data movement, not just schema structure.

questions.q: Why doesn't a developer using DACPAC deployment hand-write the ALTER TABLE statement that runs against the target?
options: SqlPackage automatically figures out the actual diff between the DACPAC and the target's current state and applies exactly that
SQL Server generates ALTER statements randomly regardless of the DACPAC
Hand-writing ALTER statements is technically disallowed in any automated pipeline
The DACPAC file already physically contains the exact statements for every possible target
questions.explain: The value of DACPAC deployment is that the diffing and script generation is automatic, based on comparing the DACPAC to the real current state of the target.
